stage2_instructions.what_to_describe:
Sensor data already covers gripper aperture, arm pose, and per-phase kinematics — don't repeat those numbers. Focus on what vision uniquely resolves:
- Wrist views: gripper STATE — is it open, closed on empty space, or actually holding an object? - Overhead view: object LAYOUT and INTER-OBJECT relations. - Any task-specific configuration cues you can see (e.g. cable still plugged in, lid resting on pot).
stage2_instructions.naming_and_vocabulary: For task-relevant objects, prefer the canonical names from the system prompt's <task_objects>; use left_gripper / right_gripper for the two arms. For spatial / contact relations, the <predicates> list there is a suggested vocabulary — use it when it fits, otherwise describe in your own words. Background props can be named freely.
stage2_instructions.output_format:
For each timestamp, emit a block matching this template. Items in [square brackets] are placeholders you fill in.
<caption t="T.TTs"> - **L**: [one short sentence about the LEFT gripper at this instant] - **H**: [one short sentence about object layout and dominant scene state] - **R**: [one short sentence about the RIGHT gripper at this instant] - **relations**: - [subject] [predicate] [object] - ... </caption>
Omit any L / H / R bullet whose view is not provided at that timestamp. Omit the relations block when nothing is in salient contact or alignment.
stage2_instructions.do_not: Do NOT speculate about motion, intent, success / failure, or what happens between frames — you are describing one instant per cell.
